items.title: Hard-coded secret
items.plain_explanation: Stripe secret key written in the source (in server.ts, line 5). Anyone who sees your code (a public repo, a leaked laptop, the browser) can use it as you, for example to charge cards or read your data.

items.title: SQL injection
items.plain_explanation: SQL query built by joining strings with user input (in server.ts, line 13). An attacker can change the query to read, change or delete everything in your database.

items.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
items.plain_explanation: Request data is written straight into the HTML response (in server.ts, line 19). An attacker can run their own JavaScript in your users' browsers and steal their sessions.

items.title: Missing security headers
items.plain_explanation: The express app sends no security headers (in server.ts, line 6). Browsers then allow clickjacking, content sniffing and make XSS easier to exploit.

items.title: CORS open to every website
items.plain_explanation: CORS allows every website to call this API (in server.ts, line 9). Other sites can make requests to your API from your users' browsers and read the answers.

1.title: Hard-coded secret
1.what: Stripe secret key written in the source (in server.ts, line 5). Anyone who sees your code (a public repo, a leaked laptop, the browser) can use it as you, for example to charge cards or read your data.
1.why_it_matters: Anyone who sees your code (a public repo, a leaked laptop, the browser) can use it as you, for example to charge cards or read your data.
1.how_to_fix: Move it to an environment variable or secrets manager, keep .env out of git, and rotate the key because it is already exposed.

3.title: SQL injection
3.what: SQL query built by joining strings with user input (in server.ts, line 13). An attacker can change the query to read, change or delete everything in your database.
3.why_it_matters: An attacker can change the query to read, change or delete everything in your database.
3.how_to_fix: Use a parameterised query (placeholders like ? or $1) and pass user values separately.

4.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
4.what: Request data is written straight into the HTML response (in server.ts, line 19). An attacker can run their own JavaScript in your users' browsers and steal their sessions.
4.why_it_matters: An attacker can run their own JavaScript in your users' browsers and steal their sessions.
4.how_to_fix: Escape output (use textContent, a template engine's auto-escaping, or a sanitiser like DOMPurify).

5.title: Missing security headers
5.what: The express app sends no security headers (in server.ts, line 6). Browsers then allow clickjacking, content sniffing and make XSS easier to exploit.
5.why_it_matters: Browsers then allow clickjacking, content sniffing and make XSS easier to exploit.
5.how_to_fix: Add a header middleware such as helmet (Express) or Flask-Talisman, or use the security_headers recipe.

2.title: CORS open to every website
2.what: CORS allows every website to call this API (in server.ts, line 9). Other sites can make requests to your API from your users' browsers and read the answers.
2.why_it_matters: Other sites can make requests to your API from your users' browsers and read the answers.
2.how_to_fix: Allow only your own front-end origins, for example from an ALLOWED_ORIGINS environment variable.
